entry.content:
Week 1 — Model the Board

Challenge series: Snake & Ladder Developer Challenge  | Week 1 of 4 Dates: 6–12 July 2026

The Setup

Every game needs a board. Before any snake can bite or ladder can lift, you need a data model that captures the state of a game — players, positions, and crucially, whose turn it is and what can happen next.

This week we will build the CDS foundation: entities, a status enum, and your first @flow.status annotation. No game logic yet — just clean modelling and a running CAP service.

What You'll Build This Week

  • A new CAP Node.js project: snake-ladder
  • CDS entities for GameSession, Player, and BoardSquare
  • A TurnStatus enum with the game states
  • Your first @flow.status annotation
  • Seed data: a 10×10 board with all snakes and ladders pre-loaded
  • A running service at http://localhost:4004

Prerequisites

  • Node.js 20+
  • @SAP/cds-dk installed globally:
npm install -g @sap/cds-dk
  • VS Code with the SAP CDS Language Support extension. Check Initial Setup for more details how to do a local setup. 

Background: CAP Status Flows in 60 Seconds

CAP's @flow.status feature turns a regular enum field into a controlled state machine. You annotate:

  • The entity with @flow.status: FieldName to designate which field drives the state machine
  • Bound actions with @from: [#StateA] to declare which states allow that action
  • Bound actions with @TO: #StateB to declare the target state after the action runs

CAP handles the rest automatically:

  • Validates the current state before the action runs (returns HTTP 409 if wrong state)
  • Updates the status field after the action completes
  • Generates Fiori annotations to enable/disable buttons based on current state

No custom validation code. No manual status updates. The framework enforces the rules.

Step-by-Step

1. Initialise the CAP project

cds init snake-ladder --nodejs
cd snake-ladder
npm install
code .

2. Create the data model

Create db/schema.cds:

namespace snakeladder;

// ── Status enum — the heart of the state machine ──────────────────────────
type TurnStatus : String enum {
  Waiting;    // Session created, not yet started
  Playing;    // It's this player's turn — roll the dice!
  Moving;     // Dice rolled, player token is being moved
  Blocked;    // Player hit a double-headed snake — skips next turn
  Finished;   // This player has reached square 100 and won
}

// ── Board square — pre-loaded with snake/ladder data ──────────────────────
entity BoardSquares {
  key square      : Integer;        // 1–100
      snakeTo     : Integer;        // 0 if no snake on this square
      ladderTo    : Integer;        // 0 if no ladder on this square
      isDoubleHead: Boolean default false;  // true if this is a double-headed snake mouth
}

// ── Game session ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
entity GameSessions {
  key ID          : UUID;
      name        : String(100);    // e.g. "Friday Afternoon Game"
      createdAt   : Timestamp;
      startedAt   : Timestamp;
      finishedAt  : Timestamp;
      winner      : Association to Players;
}

// ── Player — one row per player per session ───────────────────────────────
@flow.status: TurnStatus
entity Players {
  key ID          : UUID;
      session     : Association to GameSessions;
      name        : String(100);
      @readonly
      position    : Integer default 1;      // current square (1–100)
      @readonly
      TurnStatus  : TurnStatus default #Waiting;
      turnOrder   : Integer;                // 1 = goes first
      lastRoll    : Integer;               // last dice result
}

Why @flow.status on Players? Each player is an independent state machine. Their TurnStatus transitions independently — one player is Playing while others are Waiting.

3. Create the service

Create srv/game-service.cds:

using { snakeladder } from '../db/schema';

service GameService {

  entity GameSessions as projection on snakeladder.GameSessions;

  @flow.status: TurnStatus
  entity Players as projection on snakeladder.Players actions {

    // Week 2 will implement these — declare them now so the model is complete
    @from: [ #Waiting ]
    @to: #Playing
    action startTurn();

    @from: [ #Playing ]
    @to: #Moving
    action rollDice() returns Integer;

    @from: [ #Moving ]
    @to: #Waiting                  // transitions to next player in Week 3
    action confirmMove();

    @from: [ #Moving ]
    @to: #Blocked                  // double-headed snake bite
    action blockPlayer();

    @from: [ #Blocked ]
    @to: $flow.previous            // restores pre-block status
    action unblockPlayer();

    @from: [ #Moving ]
    @to: #Finished
    action winGame();
  }

  entity BoardSquares as projection on snakeladder.BoardSquares;
}

entry.title: 🐍 July Developer Challenge Week 2 — Roll & Move
entry.content:
Week 2 — Roll & Move

Challenge series: Snake & Ladder Developer Challenge | Week 2 of 4 Dates: 13–19 July 2026

The Setup

You have a board. You have a player state machine. This week we will make it move.

This week you implement the bound action handlers that power the game: dice rolling, position calculation, and snake/ladder logic. CAP's @flow.status machinery will automatically enforce that moves only happen in the right state — your job is to write the business logic inside each handler.

By the end of this week you can play a full single-player game from the command line using plain OData calls.

What You'll Build This Week

  • Handler implementations for rollDice, confirmMove, blockPlayer, unblockPlayer, and winGame
  • Snake and ladder position resolution (including double-headed snake logic)
  • HTTP 409 proof: demonstrating that calling an action in the wrong state is rejected by CAP
  • An end-to-end single-player run reaching square 100

How CAP Enforces State Transitions

Before your handler code runs, CAP checks the current TurnStatus of the player entity against the @from annotation on the action. If the status doesn't match, CAP returns:

HTTP/1.1 409 Conflict
{
  "error": {
    "code": "409",
    "message": "Action 'rollDice' is not allowed in current status 'Waiting'"
  }
}

No code from you. No if (status !== 'Playing') throw .... The annotation does it.

After your handler returns (without throwing), CAP updates the status field to the @TO value. Again — no code from you.

This is the key insight of the week: your handler only contains business logic, not state management.

Step-by-Step

1. Create the service implementation file

Create srv/game-service.js:

const cds = require('@sap/cds')

module.exports = class GameService extends cds.ApplicationService {
  async init() {

    const { Players, BoardSquares } = this.entities

    // ── startTurn ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    // @from: [#Waiting]  →  CAP validates status before this runs
    // @to: #Playing      →  CAP updates status after this returns
    // No business logic needed — CAP's @flow.status handles the transition.
    this.on('startTurn', 'Players', async (req) => {
      // Intentionally empty: the @from/@to annotations do all the work.
    })

    // ── rollDice ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    // @from: [#Playing]  →  CAP validates status before this runs
    // @to: #Moving       →  CAP updates status after this returns
    this.on('rollDice', 'Players', async (req) => {
      const player = await SELECT.one.from(Players).where({ ID: req.params[0].ID })
      if (!player) return req.error(404, 'Player not found')

      const roll = Math.ceil(Math.random() * 6)
      let newPosition = player.position + roll

      // Can't overshoot square 100 — must land exactly
      if (newPosition > 100) {
        await UPDATE(Players).set({ lastRoll: roll }).where({ ID: player.ID })
        const needed = 100 - player.position
        return req.reject(409, `Need exactly ${needed} to finish. Rolled ${roll}. No move.`)
      }

      // Resolve snake or ladder on the new square
      const square = await SELECT.one.from(BoardSquares).where({ square: newPosition })
      let finalPosition = newPosition
      let event = null

      if (square?.ladderTo) {
        finalPosition = square.ladderTo
        event = { type: 'ladder', 'from': newPosition, 'to': finalPosition }
      } else if (square?.snakeTo) {
        finalPosition = square.snakeTo
        event = square.isDoubleHead
          ? { type: 'doubleSnake', 'from': newPosition, 'to': finalPosition }
          : { type: 'snake', 'from': newPosition, 'to': finalPosition }
      }

      // Persist position and last roll
      await UPDATE(Players)
        .set({ position: finalPosition, lastRoll: roll })
        .where({ ID: player.ID })

      // Emit domain event so subscribers (Week 3) can react
      if (event) await this.emit('BoardEvent', { playerID: player.ID, ...event })

      // Use req.reply() — not return — to pin the response value before CAP's
      // @flow.status after-handler runs. A plain `return` gets cleared by the
      // flow machinery, producing HTTP 204 instead of the expected 200 + body.
      req.reply({ roll, position: finalPosition, event: event?.type ?? 'normal' })
    })

    // ── confirmMove ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    // @from: [#Moving]  →  normal end of a turn, hands off to next player (Week 3)
    // @to: #Waiting     →  player waits for their next turn
    this.on('confirmMove', 'Players', async (req) => {
      // Week 3 will add turn rotation here.
      // For now: just let CAP apply @to: #Waiting
    })

    // ── blockPlayer ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    // @from: [#Moving]  →  called when player lands on a double-headed snake
    // @to: #Blocked     →  player skips their next turn
    this.on('blockPlayer', 'Players', async (req) => {
      // Business logic: the position was already updated in rollDice.
      // This action just transitions state — CAP handles the @to: #Blocked update.
      req.info('Player is blocked and will skip their next turn.')
    })

    // ── unblockPlayer ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    // @from: [#Blocked]   →  called at the start of a blocked player's next turn
    // @to: $flow.previous →  CAP restores the status to whatever it was before #Blocked
    this.on('unblockPlayer', 'Players', async (req) => {
      // CAP's $flow.previous does the work — no code needed here.
      // The player's status returns to #Waiting automatically.
    })

    // ── winGame ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    // @from: [#Moving]  →  called when player.position === 100
    // @to: #Finished    →  player has won
    this.on('winGame', 'Players', async (req) => {
      const player = await SELECT.one.from(Players).where({ ID: req.params[0].ID })
      if (!player) return req.error(404, 'Player not found')

      // Mark the session as finished with this player as winner
      await UPDATE('snakeladder.GameSessions')
        .set({
          finishedAt: new Date().toISOString(),
          winner_ID: player.ID
        })
        .where({ ID: player.session_ID })

      await this.emit('GameWon', { playerID: player.ID, sessionID: player.session_ID })
    })

    return super.init()
  }
}

If you notice rollDice action response looks different from how it was defined last week.

Lets adapt it as shown in srv/game-service.cds

  @from: [ #Playing ]
  @to: #Moving
  action rollDice() returns { roll: Integer; position: Integer; event: String; };

 

2. Add the domain events to your service CDS

Add these to the bottom of srv/game-service.cds:

// Domain events — emitted by handlers, consumed in Week 3
event BoardEvent {
  playerID : UUID;
  type     : String;   // 'ladder' | 'snake' | 'doubleSnake'
  from  : Integer;  // 'from' is a CDS reserved word — escape with ![]
  ![to]    : Integer;
}

event GameWon {
  playerID  : UUID;
  sessionID : UUID;
}

An error is intentionally introduced in the snippet above with the hint.  

3. Test the state machine manually

Start the server:

cds watch

First, create a player using the REST API or the Fiori Launchpad at http://localhost:4004. Then test the status flow:

Note on service path: CAP derives the OData path from the service name. GameService maps to /odata/v4/game (lowercase, stripped of the "Service" suffix). All example requests below use this path. You can confirm the mounted path in the cds watch console output: serving GameService { at: '/odata/v4/game' }.

Step 1 — Start a turn (transitions Waiting → Playing):

POST http://localhost:4004/odata/v4/game/Players(ID=<your-player-id>)/startTurn
Content-Type: application/json
{}

Expected response: HTTP 204 No Content (empty body). This is correct — startTurn has no return type, so CAP applies the @TO: #Playing transition silently. Verify the state changed with a GET:

GET http://localhost:4004/odata/v4/game/Players(ID=<your-player-id>)?$select=TurnStatus

You should see "TurnStatus": "Playing".

Step 2 — Roll the dice (transitions Playing → Moving):

POST http://localhost:4004/odata/v4/game/Players(ID=<your-player-id>)/rollDice
Content-Type: application/json
{}

Expected response: HTTP 200 with the dice roll, new position, and board event:

{
  "@context": "$metadata#GameService.rollDiceType",
  "roll": 4,
  "position": 38,
  "event": "ladder"
}

The event field is "normal", "ladder", "snake", or "doubleSnake". The position is the final square after any snake or ladder has been applied — so you can read the outcome directly from the action response without a follow-up GET.

Why req.reply() not return? CAP's @flow.status machinery runs an after-handler that updates the status field. If you use a plain return, that after-handler clears the response value and the client gets HTTP 204 No Content instead. Calling req.reply({...}) pins the response before the flow handler runs, so the body reaches the client.

Step 3 — Prove the 409 rejection:

Without calling confirmMove first, try to call rollDice again. CAP will return:

HTTP/1.1 409 Conflict
{
  "error": {
    "code": "409",
    "message": "Action 'rollDice' is not allowed in current status 'Moving'"
  }
}

This is the framework working exactly as designed. Screenshot this — it's your Week 2 submission evidence.

Step 4 — Confirm the move (transitions Moving → Waiting):

POST http://localhost:4004/odata/v4/game/Players(ID=<your-player-id>)/confirmMove
Content-Type: application/json
{}

Expected response: HTTP 204 No Content (empty body). confirmMove has no return type — the empty response is correct. Verify with a GET that TurnStatus is now "Waiting".

4. Test the double-headed snake

Manually set a player to position 88 (one roll away from square 89, a double-headed snake head):

PATCH http://localhost:4004/odata/v4/game/Players(ID=<your-player-id>)
Content-Type: application/json
{ "position": 88 }

Note: position is @readonly in the service — for testing, update it directly via the db entity or temporarily remove @readonly.

remove @readonly from srv/game-service.cds for testing, and note that patching @readonly fields fails silently with HTTP 200.

Then start a turn and roll — if you roll 1, you land on 89 (a double-headed snake head). Your position should move to 50 (the shared tail). The BoardEvent event should fire with type: 'doubleSnake'.

Follow up by calling blockPlayer to transition to #Blocked, then unblockPlayer to see $flow.previous restore the state.

The $flow.previous Moment

When you call unblockPlayer and see the status return to its previous value automatically — that's CAP's state history at work. No code, no stored "previousStatus" field. The framework tracks it.

Note: $flow.previous restores whatever status the entity held before the transition to #Blocked. In this flow, blockPlayer is called from #Moving, so unblockPlayer restores #Moving — not #Waiting. The game loop then calls confirmMove to finish the turn. If you call blockPlayer from a different status in future extensions, $flow.previous will restore that one instead.

Stretch Goal

Add a skipTurn action that can be called when a player is #Blocked, as an alternative to unblockPlayer, that uses @TO: $flow.previous as well but also increments a turnsBlocked counter on the player:

@from: [ #Blocked ]
@to: $flow.previous
action skipTurn();
this.on('skipTurn', 'Players', async (req) => {
  const player = await SELECT.one.from(Players).where({ ID: req.params[0].ID })
  await UPDATE(Players)
    .set({ turnsBlocked: (player.turnsBlocked || 0) + 1 })
    .where({ ID: player.ID })
})

How to Submit

Reply to the Week 2 blog post on SAP Community with a comment containing:

  1. Your srv/game-service.js handler implementations (paste as a JS code block)
  2. A screenshot showing the HTTP 409 response when calling rollDice in the wrong state
  3. A screenshot or OData response showing your player's position after landing on a snake or ladder
  4. One sentence: what happens if you call winGame on a player whose position is not 100? How does your implementation handle it?

What's Next

In Week 3 — Multiplayer & Events, you add a second player, implement turn rotation, and wire up a CAP event subscriber that automatically advances the game state when a move is confirmed.

entry.title: 🐍 July Developer Challenge Week 3 — Multiplayer & Events
entry.content:
Week 3 — Multiplayer & Events

Challenge series: Snake & Ladder Developer Challenge | Week 3 of 4 Dates: 20–26 July 2026

The Setup

A single-player Snake & Ladder game is a solitaire puzzle. The real game is multiplayer — taking turns, watching opponents climb ladders, celebrating when a snake bites someone ahead of you.

This week you add a second player, implement turn rotation, and wire CAP events so the game state advances automatically. You'll also use the CAP MCP server to let an AI assistant watch the game — describing what happened on each turn in natural language.

What You'll Build This Week

  • Turn rotation: confirmMove activates the next player automatically
  • A GameSession state machine (separate from Player status)
  • A CAP event subscriber that drives turn handoff
  • A TurnLog entity recording every move for replay
  • CAP MCP server connected to the game — so an AI can query board state and narrate moves

Background: CAP Events as the Turn Engine

CAP events let services communicate without tight coupling. Your GameService emits a BoardEvent when a player moves. A subscriber — in the same service or a separate one — reacts to that event and advances the game.

CAP messaging key facts :

  • this.emit(eventName, data) inside an action handler automatically fires after the DB transaction commits — no manual outbox needed for in-process events.
  • This week uses in-process eventing (same cds watch process). If you later split into microservices, add file-based-messaging to package.json and your handler code stays unchanged — only the config changes.

This is the architecture for multiplayer:

Player calls rollDice
  → CAP validates @from: [#Playing]
  → Handler runs: calculates new position, emits BoardEvent
  → CAP applies @to: #Moving
  → Player calls confirmMove
  → CAP validates @from: [#Moving]
  → Handler emits TurnComplete event
  → CAP applies @to: #Waiting
  → TurnComplete subscriber: logs the turn (next-player activation already done inside confirmMove)

No polling. No setInterval. The event graph drives the game.

Step-by-Step

0. Upgrade to the latest CAP version

Before adding Week 3 features, upgrade your project to the latest @SAP/cds. CAP 10 brings performance improvements, refined flow-status behaviour, and updated MCP support.

If you skipped Week 2's CDS 10 note: cds init --nodejs in CDS 10 generates "type": "module" in package.json. The handler code in these guides uses CommonJS require(). If your server crashes with ReferenceError: require is not defined, remove "type": "module" from package.json. Running npm install @sap/cds@latest also removes it automatically.

npm install @sap/cds@latest @cap-js/mcp@latest @cap-js/sqlite@latest

Verify the versions installed:

cds --version

You should see @SAP/cds at 10.x or higher. Restart cds watch — if the service starts cleanly, you're ready.

Global CLI: The cds command comes from @sap/cds-dk. Keep it in sync:

npm install -g @sap/cds-dk@latest

1. Add the TurnLog entity

Add to db/schema.cds:

// ── Turn log — full history of every move ─────────────────────────────────
entity TurnLog {
  key ID          : UUID;
      session     : Association to GameSessions;
      player      : Association to Players;
      turnNumber  : Integer;
      diceRoll    : Integer;
      fromSquare  : Integer;
      toSquare    : Integer;
      eventType   : String(20);   // 'normal' | 'ladder' | 'snake' | 'doubleSnake' | 'win' | 'blocked'
      timestamp   : Timestamp;
}

Also update the Players entity in db/schema.cds to add these two fields needed by the confirmMove handler:

prevPosition  : Integer default 1;    // position before last dice roll
lastEventType : String(20);           // event from last roll: normal|ladder|snake|doubleSnake

Add it to srv/game-service.cds — inside the service GameService { } block, before the closing brace:

entity TurnLog as projection on snakeladder.TurnLog;

And add the TurnComplete event — also inside the service block so it appears in OData $metadata and the MCP describe tool:

event TurnComplete {
  sessionID    : UUID;
  playerID     : UUID;
  nextPlayerID : UUID;
  turnNumber   : Integer;
}

2. Implement turn rotation in the handler

Update srv/game-service.js — replace confirmMove and add the TurnComplete subscriber:

Before implementing confirmMove: Your Week 2 rollDice handler must store two additional fields during the UPDATE(Players) call. If you haven't already, add these to the .set({...}) block in rollDice:

prevPosition: player.position,     // position BEFORE the move (used for TurnLog)
lastEventType: event?.type ?? 'normal'  // ladder/snake/doubleSnake/normal

These are read by confirmMove when writing the TurnLog entry.

// ── confirmMove ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// After this returns, CAP sets status → #Waiting.
// We then find the next player and set them to #Playing.
this.on('confirmMove', 'Players', async (req) => {
  // Players and TurnLog are already destructured at the top of init()
  const player = await SELECT.one.from(Players).where({ ID: req.params[0].ID })
  if (!player) return req.error(404, 'Player not found')

  // ── Check win condition before handing off ──
  if (player.position === 100) {
    // Delegate to winGame — correct CAP bound-action call syntax
    await this.send({ event: 'winGame', entity: 'Players', params: [{ ID: player.ID }] })
    return
  }

  // ── Log this turn ──
  const [{ n: count }] = await SELECT`count(*) as n`.from(TurnLog)
    .where({ session_ID: player.session_ID })
  const turnNumber = (count || 0) + 1
  await INSERT.into(TurnLog).entries({
    ID: cds.utils.uuid(),
    session_ID: player.session_ID,
    player_ID: player.ID,
    turnNumber,
    diceRoll: player.lastRoll,
    fromSquare: player.prevPosition,            // pre-roll position stored by rollDice
    toSquare: player.position,
    eventType: player.lastEventType ?? 'normal', // event type stored by rollDice
    timestamp: new Date().toISOString()
  })

  // ── Find next player in turn order ──
  const players = await SELECT.from(Players)
    .where({ session_ID: player.session_ID })
    .orderBy('turnOrder')

  const idx = players.findIndex(p => p.ID === player.ID)
  // Skip finished players — guard counter prevents infinite loop if all finish simultaneously
  let nextIdx = (idx + 1) % players.length
  let guard = 0
  while (players[nextIdx].TurnStatus === 'Finished' && guard++ < players.length) {
    nextIdx = (nextIdx + 1) % players.length
  }
  const next = players[nextIdx]

  await this.emit('TurnComplete', {
    sessionID: player.session_ID,
    playerID: player.ID,
    nextPlayerID: next.ID,
    turnNumber
  })

  // Activate next player — use direct UPDATE, not the flow action,
  // because we're already inside a handler
  await UPDATE(Players)
    .set({ TurnStatus: 'Playing' })
    .where({ ID: next.ID })
})

// ── TurnComplete event subscriber ─────────────────────────────────────────
// NOTE: this.after() on custom events receives (handlerResult, req) — the
// first argument is undefined (no return value from the event). Use req.data.
this.after('TurnComplete', async (_results, req) => {
  const data = req.data
  console.log(`[TurnComplete] session=${data.sessionID} nextPlayer=${data.nextPlayerID} turn=${data.turnNumber}`)
})

3. Add a session-level startGame action

Players need a way to transition a session from "lobby" to "in progress". Add to db/schema.cds:

type SessionStatus : String enum {
  Lobby;      // Accepting players, not yet started
  InProgress; // Game is running
  Complete;   // A player has won
}

@flow.status: SessionStatus
entity GameSessions {
  key ID          : UUID;
      name        : String(100);
      @cds.on.insert: $now
      createdAt   : Timestamp;
      startedAt   : Timestamp;
      finishedAt  : Timestamp;
      winner      : Association to Players;
      @readonly
      SessionStatus : SessionStatus default #Lobby;
}

Add to srv/game-service.cds actions on GameSessions:

@flow.status: SessionStatus
entity GameSessions as projection on snakeladder.GameSessions actions {

  @from: [ #Lobby ]
  @to: #InProgress
  action startGame();

  @from: [ #InProgress ]
  @to: #Complete
  action endGame();
}

Also verify startTurn is still in your Players actions from Week 2. If you rebuilt your service file, make sure it includes:

@from: [ #Waiting ]
@to: #Playing
action startTurn();

In the multiplayer flow, startGame sets the first player directly to Playing, and confirmMove advances turns via direct UPDATE — so startTurn is not strictly required for multiplayer turn rotation. However, it's still useful for manual testing and for single-player Week 2 scenarios. Keep it in your service definition.

Implement startGame in game-service.js:

// Players, BoardSquares, TurnLog are already destructured at the top of init()
// Make sure your top-of-init destructure includes ALL three:
// const { Players, BoardSquares, TurnLog } = this.entities
this.on('startGame', 'GameSessions', async (req) => {
  const sessionID = req.params[0].ID

  // All players start in Waiting — set the first in turn order to Playing
  const players = await SELECT.from(Players)
    .where({ session_ID: sessionID })
    .orderBy('turnOrder')

  if (players.length < 2) {
    return req.reject(400, 'A game needs at least 2 players to start.')
  }

  await UPDATE(Players)
    .set({ TurnStatus: 'Playing' })
    .where({ ID: players[0].ID })

  await UPDATE('snakeladder.GameSessions')
    .set({ startedAt: new Date().toISOString() })
    .where({ ID: sessionID })
})

Also add the endGame handler. This action is triggered by the @flow.status machinery (it transitions SessionStatus to #Complete automatically), but it must also set finishedAt:

this.on('endGame', 'GameSessions', async (req) => {
  await UPDATE('snakeladder.GameSessions')
    .set({ finishedAt: new Date().toISOString() })
    .where({ ID: req.params[0].ID })
})

4. Test multiplayer turn rotation

Create a session with two players and start the game:

Tip: Omit the ID field in POST bodies — CAP auto-generates a UUID. Copy the returned ID from each response to use in subsequent requests.

POST http://localhost:4004/odata/v4/game/GameSessions
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "name": "My First Multiplayer Game"
}
POST http://localhost:4004/odata/v4/game/Players
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "session_ID": "<session-ID-from-above>",
  "name": "Alice",
  "turnOrder": 1
}
POST http://localhost:4004/odata/v4/game/Players
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "session_ID": "<session-ID-from-above>",
  "name": "Bob",
  "turnOrder": 2
}
POST http://localhost:4004/odata/v4/game/GameSessions(<session-ID>)/startGame
Content-Type: application/json
{}

Now Alice should be #Playing and Bob should be #Waiting. Roll for Alice, confirm her move, and Bob should automatically become #Playing.

Note on service path: CAP maps GameService to /odata/v4/game. Replace GameService in all URLs with game. See the Week 1 note for details.

Verify by checking both players' statuses after confirmMove:

GET http://localhost:4004/odata/v4/game/Players?$filter=session_ID eq '<session-ID>'

5. Connect the CAP MCP Server

The CAP MCP server exposes your GameService as tools that any MCP-compatible AI assistant (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Opencode) can call. The AI can query board state, roll dice, narrate turns — all via natural language.

Install

npm add @cap-js/mcp

That's it. No extra configuration needed. @cap-js/mcp auto-detects CAP services during cds watch.

Annotate GameService

Add @McP to your service declaration in srv/game-service.cds, plus @title and @description on entities and actions so the AI understands the game domain:

This shows only the annotations to add — keep your existing action definitions unchanged. The // ... other actions placeholder represents your existing rollDice, confirmMove, etc.

/**
 * Snake & Ladder Game Service — multiplayer board game engine.
 * Players take turns rolling dice and moving tokens across a 10×10 board.
 * Snakes send players back; ladders advance them. First to reach square 100 wins.
 */
@mcp
@protocol: ['odata-v4', 'mcp']   // keep OData alongside MCP — REQUIRED or OData drops
@title: 'Snake & Ladder Game'
service GameService {

  @title: 'Game Sessions'
  @description: 'Create a session, add players, then call startGame. SessionStatus: Lobby → InProgress → Complete.'
  @flow.status: SessionStatus
  entity GameSessions as projection on snakeladder.GameSessions actions {
    /** Start the game. Requires at least 2 players. Sets first player (turnOrder=1) to Playing. */
    @from: [ #Lobby ] @to: #InProgress
    action startGame();
    // ... other actions
  }

  @title: 'Players'
  @description: 'Each player has a position (1-100) and TurnStatus. Call rollDice when Playing, then confirmMove to end the turn.'
  @flow.status: TurnStatus
  @cds.redirection.target
  entity Players as projection on snakeladder.Players actions {
    /**
     * Roll a 6-sided dice and move the player.
     * Returns: roll (1-6), position (new square after snakes/ladders), event (normal/ladder/snake/doubleSnake).
     */
    @from: [ #Playing ] @to: #Moving
    action rollDice() returns { roll: Integer; position: Integer; event: String; };
    // ... other actions
  }

  @title: 'Board State'
  @description: 'Live view of all player positions. Filter by session_ID to see a specific game.'
  @readonly
  entity BoardState as select from snakeladder.Players {
    key ID,
    name, position, TurnStatus, lastRoll,
    session.ID   as session_ID : UUID,   // typed alias — makes session_ID OData-filterable
    session.name as sessionName
  };
}

Start cds watch and the MCP endpoint appears automatically

cds watch

Look for this line in the output:

[cds] - serving GameService {
  at: [ '/odata/v4/game', '/mcp/game' ],
  ...
}

The MCP server is live at http://localhost:4004/mcp/game.

Add MCP-callable wrapper functions

The @cap-js/mcp query tool reads data; bound actions on entities (like rollDice) aren't directly callable by the AI. Add unbound service functions that the AI can call via per_action_tool. Add these to srv/game-service.cds inside the service block:

// ── MCP-callable unbound functions — allow AI to drive the game ──────────
/** Start a game session. Requires sessionID of a Lobby session with ≥2 players. */
function mcpStartGame(sessionID: UUID) returns String;

/** Roll the dice for the current Playing player. */
function mcpRollDice(playerID: UUID) returns { roll: Integer; position: Integer; event: String; };

/** Confirm a move and rotate the turn to the next player. */
function mcpConfirmMove(playerID: UUID) returns String;

/** Get the current board state for a game session. */
function mcpBoardState(sessionID: UUID) returns array of {
  name: String; position: Integer; TurnStatus: String; lastRoll: Integer;
};

/** All 100 squares with snake/ladder info. */
function mcpBoardMap() returns array of {
  square: Integer; snakeTo: Integer; ladderTo: Integer; isDoubleHead: Boolean;
};

Implement them in srv/game-service.js (add before return super.init()😞

Critical: use the object form of this.send() for bound entity actions. The string form this.send('rollDice', { params }) puts { params } into req.data of the dispatched request — bound action handlers read the entity key from req.params[0].ID, which will be undefined. Your handlers will run silently returning success but touching nothing. Always use the object form:

// ✗ WRONG — params land in req.data, req.params is empty
await this.send('rollDice', { params: [{ ID: playerID }] })

// ✓ CORRECT — params routed to req.params[0]
await this.send({ event: 'rollDice', entity: 'Players', params: [{ ID: playerID }] })
this.on('mcpStartGame', async (req) => {
  // Use object form: string form puts params in req.data, not req.params
  await this.send({ event: 'startGame', entity: 'GameSessions', params: [{ ID: req.data.sessionID }] })
  return `Game started for session ${req.data.sessionID}`
})
this.on('mcpRollDice', async (req) => {
  return await this.send({ event: 'rollDice', entity: 'Players', params: [{ ID: req.data.playerID }] })
})
this.on('mcpConfirmMove', async (req) => {
  await this.send({ event: 'confirmMove', entity: 'Players', params: [{ ID: req.data.playerID }] })
  return `Move confirmed for player ${req.data.playerID}`
})
this.on('mcpBoardState', async (req) => {
  return await SELECT.from(Players).where({ session_ID: req.data.sessionID })
    .columns('name','position','TurnStatus','lastRoll').orderBy('turnOrder')
})
this.on('mcpBoardMap', async () => SELECT.from(BoardSquares).orderBy('square'))

Enable per_action_tool in package.json:

{
  "cds": {
    "mcp": { "per_action_tool": true }
  }
}

After restarting, the MCP server exposes 7 tools: describe, query, mcpStartGame, mcpRollDice, mcpConfirmMove, mcpBoardState, mcpBoardMap.

 

Note: You can use any MCP tool of your choice. 

Use with Claude Code (auto-wired — just ask)

With cds watch running, open a new terminal and ask Claude Code directly:

claude "What is the current board state? Who is in the lead?"

claude "Show me the turn history for the most recent game session."

claude "Which squares have snakes and which have ladders? Summarise the dangerous zones."

Claude Code uses the query and describe MCP tools to read your live game data and answer.

Use with Claude Desktop (manual wiring)

If you want the AI to also roll dice and make moves, connect Claude Desktop. Add to claude_desktop_config.json (macOS: ~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json😞

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "snake-ladder": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "mcp-remote", "http://localhost:4004/mcp/game"]
    }
  }
}

Restart Claude Desktop, then try:

"What is the current board state for the active game? Who is winning?"

"Roll the dice for the current Playing player and tell me what happened."

"Narrate the last 5 turns like a sports commentator."

Verify the MCP endpoint — tools list and action tests

Step 1 — List all tools (should be exactly 7):

curl -X POST http://localhost:4004/mcp/game \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Accept: application/json, text/event-stream" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list","params":{}}'

Expected: SSE response with tools array containing query, describe, mcpStartGame, mcpRollDice, mcpConfirmMove, mcpBoardState, mcpBoardMap.

Step 2 — mcpBoardMap (no session needed):

curl -X POST http://localhost:4004/mcp/game \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Accept: application/json, text/event-stream" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"mcpBoardMap","arguments":{}}}'

Expected: 100 squares with snakeTo, ladderTo, isDoubleHead fields.

Step 3 — mcpStartGame (use an existing Lobby session ID):

curl -X POST http://localhost:4004/mcp/game \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Accept: application/json, text/event-stream" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"mcpStartGame","arguments":{"sessionID":"<your-session-id>"}}}'

Expected response: "result": "Game started for session ...". Then verify with OData:

GET http://localhost:4004/odata/v4/game/GameSessions(<session-id>)?$select=SessionStatus,startedAt

SessionStatus should be "InProgress" and startedAt not null.

If mcpStartGame returns success but SessionStatus stays Lobby, you have the this.send() bug — the string form was used instead of the object form. See the critical note above.

Step 4 — mcpRollDice (use the Playing player's ID):

curl -X POST http://localhost:4004/mcp/game \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Accept: application/json, text/event-stream" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":4,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"mcpRollDice","arguments":{"playerID":"<alice-id>"}}}'

Expected: {"roll":N, "position":M, "event":"normal|ladder|snake|doubleSnake"}. If you get "result": null, the this.send() object form is not being used.

Step 5 — mcpConfirmMove:

curl -X POST http://localhost:4004/mcp/game \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Accept: application/json, text/event-stream" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":5,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"mcpConfirmMove","arguments":{"playerID":"<alice-id>"}}}'

Expected: "result": "Move confirmed for player ...". Check Bob's TurnStatus is now "Playing".

Step 6 — mcpBoardState:

curl -X POST http://localhost:4004/mcp/game \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Accept: application/json, text/event-stream" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":6,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"mcpBoardState","arguments":{"sessionID":"<your-session-id>"}}}'

Expected: array of players with name, position, TurnStatus, lastRoll.

MCP uses SSE transport — responses arrive as event: message\ndata: {...}. Strip the data: prefix to parse JSON. HTTP clients that don't support SSE (like some REST clients) will show the raw text.

Understanding the Two State Machines

After this week you have two independent status flows running in your service:

Entity Field States Purpose

GameSessionsSessionStatusLobby → InProgress → CompleteGoverns the game lifecycle
PlayersTurnStatusWaiting → Playing → Moving → Blocked / FinishedGoverns each player's turn

The session state machine controls whether the game is happening. The player state machine controls whose turn it is and what they can do. CAP enforces both independently with their own @flow.status annotations.

Stretch Goal

Add a skipTurn action that a blocked player can call as an alternative to unblockPlayer, which also records how many turns they've been blocked:

@from: [ #Blocked ]
@to: $flow.previous
action skipTurn();
this.on('skipTurn', 'Players', async (req) => {
  const player = await SELECT.one.from(Players).where({ ID: req.params[0].ID })
  await UPDATE(Players)
    .set({ turnsBlocked: (player.turnsBlocked || 0) + 1 })
    .where({ ID: player.ID })
})

Note: BoardState is already included as a required entity in Step 5 (inside the @mcp-annotated service). The @cds.on.insert: $now annotation on GameSessions.createdAt coexists correctly with the Week 1 seed CSV — CAP uses the annotation for programmatic inserts but still honours explicit values in seed files.

How to Submit

Reply to the Week 3 blog post on SAP Community with a comment containing:

  1. A screenshot or JSON response showing two players after confirmMove — one Waiting, one Playing
  2. A screenshot or curl response showing mcpRollDice returning {roll, position, event} (not null) — proves the MCP action tools are wired correctly
  3. A screenshot of Claude Code or Claude Desktop ( or any MCP tool client of your choice) querying your game state via MCP — even a simple "who is winning?" response counts
  4. Optional but celebrated: a short AI-narrated turn log using mcpBoardState + TurnLog

What's Next

In Week 4 — Fiori UI & CAP MCP, you wire up the ready-made board UI, add your service URL to see your live game on a real Snake & Ladder board to complete the challenge.

Resources

  • CAP Status Flows Documentation
  • CAP MCP Server
  • CAP Node.js Events

entry.title: 🐍 July Developer Challenge Week 4 — UI & CAP MCP
entry.content:
Week 4 — UI & CAP MCP

Challenge series: Snake & Ladder Developer Challenge | Week 4 of 4 Dates: 27–31 July 2026

The Setup

The engine is built. The game works. Now you make it visible.

This week you plug your running CAP service into the provided board UI — a single HTML file that renders the live 10×10 board, shows player positions, and drives moves through your OData endpoints. No frontend coding required: just paste your service URL.

You then run the Verify Service — an automated checker that calls your service end-to-end, validates every status-flow transition, and marks your challenge complete.

And as a final flourish, you use the CAP MCP server to let an AI play an entire game against a human — or against itself.

What You'll Build This Week

  • Board UI connected to your live CAP service
  • Deploy to SAP BTP Cloud Foundry (or keep it local — both count)
  • Run the Verify Service and get your completion badge
  • An AI-vs-human or AI-vs-AI demo using CAP MCP

Part 1: The Board UI

The Board UI is a single self-contained HTML file — no npm, no build, no git clone required. Copy the full source below, save it as index.html, open it in a browser, paste your service URL, and connect.

What the UI does

  • Renders the full 10×10 board using the realistic snake board image — gold ladders, green single-head snakes, purple double-head snakes
  • Active Sessions panel — shows all live games after Connect, with status badges (▶ Playing, ⬤ Lobby, ✓ Done), player count, and time
  • New Game step-by-step flow — Step 1: create an empty session; Step 2: add players one by one (Enter key or + Add button); Step 3: Start Game — all without leaving the browser
  • Join / Watch / Delete — click any session row to load it on the board; 🗑 delete cascades to all players
  • Shows each player's token at their current position (canvas overlay on the board image)
  • Highlights whose turn it is (TurnStatus: Playing)
  • Has a Roll Dice button that calls your rollDice action
  • Has a Confirm Move button that calls confirmMove
  • Polls GET /Players every 3 seconds so a second browser tab (simulating player 2) stays in sync
  • Shows a Turn Log panel with the last 10 moves
  • Seed/demo sessions (no createdAt) are automatically hidden from the list

Board UI — Full Source Code

Copy the entire block below, save as index.html, open in your browser:

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
<meta charset="UTF-8">
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
<title>Snake & Ladder — SAP Developer Challenge</title>
<style>  :root {
    --navy:   #1D2D68;
    --blue:   #0070F2;
    --teal:   #00D9BE;
    --mag:    #E8106E;
    --purple: #7B2FBE;
    --dark:   #0D1B4B;
    --cellA:  #D0E4FF;
    --cellB:  #EEF4FF;
    --border: #6090C8;
    --text:   #0D1B4B;
  }
  * { box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0; padding: 0; }
  body {
    background: linear-gradient(135deg, var(--dark) 0%, var(--navy) 100%);
    font-family: 'Segoe UI', Arial, sans-serif;
    color: #fff;
    min-height: 100vh;
    padding: 16px;
  }
  /* ── Header ── */
  .header {
    display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between;
    margin-bottom: 14px;
  }
  .header h1 { font-size: 1.4rem; color: var(--teal); }
  .header p  { font-size: 0.78rem; color: #a0b8e8; margin-top: 2px; }
  .sap-logo  { background: var(--blue); color: #fff; font-weight: 900; font-size: 1.2rem; padding: 5px 12px; border-radius: 5px; }

  /* ── Layout ── */
  .layout { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 520px 1fr; gap: 16px; align-items: start; }
  canvas   { display: block; }

  /* ── Panel ── */
  .panel { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 12px; }
  .card  { background: rgba(255,255,255,.06); border: 1px solid rgba(0,112,242,.35); border-radius: 8px; padding: 14px 16px; }
  .card h3 { font-size: .7rem; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 1.5px; color: var(--teal); margin-bottom: 10px; }

  /* ── Connect form ── */
  .field { margin-bottom: 8px; }
  .field label { font-size: .7rem; color: #a0b8e8; display: block; margin-bottom: 4px; }
  .field input  {
    width: 100%; background: rgba(0,0,0,.3); border: 1px solid rgba(0,112,242,.5);
    border-radius: 5px; color: #d0e8ff; padding: 7px 9px; font-size: .78rem;
    font-family: 'Courier New', monospace; outline: none;
  }
  .field input:focus { border-color: var(--teal); }
  .field input::placeholder { color: #4a6a9a; }
  .btn-row { display: flex; gap: 8px; margin-top: 4px; }
  .btn {
    padding: 7px 14px; border-radius: 5px; border: none; cursor: pointer;
    font-size: .78rem; font-weight: 600; transition: opacity .15s;
  }
  .btn:hover { opacity: .85; }
  .btn-primary { background: var(--blue);  color: #fff; }
  .btn-teal    { background: var(--teal);  color: var(--dark); }
  .btn-mag     { background: var(--mag);   color: #fff; }
  .btn-purple  { background: var(--purple);color: #fff; }
  .btn:disabled { opacity: .4; cursor: not-allowed; }

  /* ── Status badge ── */
  .conn-status { font-size: .72rem; margin-top: 6px; }
  .conn-status.ok  { color: var(--teal); }
  .conn-status.err { color: var(--mag); }
  .conn-status.inf { color: #a0b8e8; }

  /* ── Players list ── */
  .player-row {
    display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px;
    padding: 8px 0; border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.06);
  }
  .player-row:last-child { border-bottom: none; }
  .avatar {
    width: 32px; height: 32px; border-radius: 50%;
    display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;
    font-weight: bold; font-size: .8rem; flex-shrink: 0;
  }
  .p-info { flex: 1; }
  .p-name { font-size: .88rem; font-weight: 600; }
  .p-pos  { font-size: .7rem; color: #a0b8e8; }
  .p-badge {
    font-size: .66rem; font-weight: bold; padding: 3px 8px;
    border-radius: 10px; white-space: nowrap;
  }
  .badge-playing  { background: rgba(0,112,242,.35); color: #90c4ff; }
  .badge-waiting  { background: rgba(255,255,255,.1); color: #a0b8e8; }
  .badge-moving   { background: rgba(0,217,190,.2);   color: var(--teal); }
  .badge-blocked  { background: rgba(232,16,110,.25); color: #ffaacc; }
  .badge-finished { background: rgba(0,217,190,.3);   color: var(--teal); }

  /* ── Action bar ── */

<script>// ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// Board uses a pre-rendered PNG (board.png / snake-ladder-board-realistic-snakes.png)
// The canvas overlay only draws player tokens on top.
// ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
const PLAYER_COLORS = ['#E8106E','#7B2FBE','#0070F2','#F97316'];

const canvas = document.getElementById('board');
const ctx    = canvas.getContext('2d');
const CELL   = canvas.width / 10;   // 52px per cell at 520px

// Map square number (1-100) to canvas centre coordinates
function cellXY(n) {
  const idx=n-1, row=Math.floor(idx/10), col=idx%10;
  const bRow=9-row, bCol=row%2===0?col:9-col;
  return { cx: bCol*CELL+CELL/2, cy: bRow*CELL+CELL/2 };
}

function drawToken(square, color, label, offX, offY) {
  const {cx,cy} = cellXY(square);
  const x = cx+offX, y = cy+(offY||CELL*0.12);
  // Drop shadow
  ctx.save();
  ctx.shadowColor = 'rgba(0,0,0,0.55)'; ctx.shadowBlur = 8; ctx.shadowOffsetY = 2;
  ctx.fillStyle = color;
  ctx.strokeStyle = '#fff'; ctx.lineWidth = 2;
  ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(x, y, CELL*0.18, 0, Math.PI*2); ctx.fill(); ctx.stroke();
  ctx.restore();
  // Label
  ctx.fillStyle = '#fff';
  ctx.font = `bold ${CELL*.14}px Segoe UI`;
  ctx.textAlign = 'center'; ctx.textBaseline = 'middle';
  ctx.fillText(label, x, y);
}

let players = [];

function renderBoard() {
  // Clear the token overlay (PNG board remains underneath)
  ctx.clearRect(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height);
  // Draw player tokens — spread them if multiple on same square
  const bySquare = {};
  players.forEach(p => { (bySquare[p.position] = bySquare[p.position]||[]).push(p); });
  Object.entries(bySquare).forEach(([sq, ps]) => {
    const offsets = ps.length===1?[0]:ps.length===2?[-9,9]:ps.length===3?[-12,0,12]:[-14,-5,5,14];
    ps.forEach((p, i) => {
      drawToken(Number(sq), PLAYER_COLORS[p._colorIdx % PLAYER_COLORS.length],
        p.name.substring(0,2).toUpperCase(), offsets[i]||0);
    });
  });
}

// ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// API integration
// ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
let serviceUrl = '';
let sessionId  = '';
let pollTimer  = null;

function getUrl(path) { return serviceUrl.replace(/\/+$/,'') + path; }

async function apiFetch(path, options = {}) {
  const isWrite = options.method && options.method !== 'GET' && options.method !== 'HEAD';
  const headers = { 'Accept': 'application/json', ...(isWrite ? { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } : {}) };
  const res = await fetch(getUrl(path), { headers, ...options });
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}: ${await res.text()}`);
  return res.json().catch(() => ({}));
}

async function connect() {
  serviceUrl = document.getElementById('serviceUrl').value.trim();
  sessionId  = '';
  const el = document.getElementById('connStatus');
  el.className = 'conn-status inf'; el.textContent = 'Connecting…';
  try {
    await apiFetch('/$metadata');
    el.className = 'conn-status ok'; el.textContent = '✓ Connected';
    document.getElementById('refreshBtn').disabled = false;
    document.getElementById('verifyUrl').value = serviceUrl;
    // Show sessions list
    document.getElementById('sessionsCard').style.display = '';
    document.getElementById('setupCard').style.display = 'none';
    await loadSessions();
  } catch(e) {
    el.className='conn-status err'; el.textContent='✕ '+e.message;
  }
}

async function loadSessions() {
  // Auto-read URL if not set
  if (!serviceUrl) serviceUrl = document.getElementById('serviceUrl').value.trim();
  if (!serviceUrl) return;
  const el = document.getElementById('sessionsList');
  el.innerHTML = '<p style="font-size:.78rem;color:#a0b8e8">Loading…</p>';
  try {
    const data = await apiFetch('/GameSessions?$orderby=createdAt desc&$top=20');
    // Filter out seed/demo sessions (no createdAt = came from CSV seed data)
    const sessions = (data.value || []).filter(s => s.createdAt);
    if (!sessions.length) {
      el.innerHTML = '<p style="font-size:.78rem;color:#a0b8e8">No sessions yet. Create one below.</p>';
      return;
    }
    // For each session, get player count
    const rows = await Promise.all(sessions.map(async s => {
      let playerCount = 0;
      try {
        const pd = await apiFetch(`/Players?$filter=session_ID eq '${s.ID}'&$count=true&$top=0`);
        playerCount = pd['@odata.count'] ?? 0;
      } catch(_) {}
      return { ...s, playerCount };
    }));

    el.innerHTML = rows.map(s => {
      const isInProgress = s.SessionStatus === 'InProgress';
      const isLobby = s.SessionStatus === 'Lobby';
      const isDone = s.SessionStatus === 'Complete';
      const rowCls = isInProgress ? 'active-game' : isLobby ? 'lobby-game' : 'done-game';
      const badgeCls = isInProgress ? 's-badge-playing' : isLobby ? 's-badge-lobby' : 's-badge-complete';
      const badgeTxt = isInProgress ? '▶ Playing' : isLobby ? '⬤ Lobby' : '✓ Done';
      const joinLabel = isDone ? 'View' : isLobby ? 'Join' : 'Watch';
      const joinColor = isDone ? 'btn-purple' : isLobby ? 'btn-mag' : 'btn-teal';
      const created = s.createdAt ? new Date(s.createdAt).toLocaleTimeString([], {hour:'2-digit',minute:'2-digit'}) : '';
      return `<div class="session-row ${rowCls}" onclick="joinSession('${s.ID}')">
        <div class="s-info">
          <div class="s-name">${s.name||'Unnamed Game'}</div>
          <div class="s-meta">${s.playerCount} player${s.playerCount!==1?'s':''} · ${created||'—'}</div>
        </div>
        <span class="s-badge ${badgeCls}">${badgeTxt}</span>
        <button class="btn ${joinColor}" onclick="event.stopPropagation();joinSession('${s.ID}')"
          style="padding:4px 10px;font-size:.72rem">${joinLabel}</button>
        <button class="btn btn-mag" title="Delete session"
          onclick="event.stopPropagation();deleteSession('${s.ID}','${(s.name||'this session').replace(/'/g,'')}')"
          style="padding:4px 8px;font-size:.72rem;opacity:.75" onmouseover="this.style.opacity=1" onmouseout="this.style.opacity=.75">🗑</button>
      </div>`;
    }).join('');
  } catch(e) {
    el.innerHTML = `<p style="font-size:.78rem;color:var(--mag)">✕ ${e.message}</p>`;
  }
}

function showNewGame() {
  // Auto-read URL if not already connected
  if (!serviceUrl) serviceUrl = document.getElementById('serviceUrl').value.trim();
  document.getElementById('setupCard').style.display = '';
  document.getElementById('setupCard').style.opacity = '1';
  document.getElementById('setupCard').style.pointerEvents = '';
  document.getElementById('stepCreateSession').style.display = '';
  document.getElementById('stepAddPlayers').style.display = 'none';
  document.getElementById('sessionCreateStatus').textContent = '';
  document.getElementById('setupSessionName').focus();
}

async function deleteSession(sid, name) {
  // Guard: ensure serviceUrl is set
  serviceUrl = serviceUrl || document.getElementById('serviceUrl').value.trim();
  if (!serviceUrl) { alert('Not connected to a service.'); return; }
  if (!confirm(`Delete "${name}"?\n\nThis will remove the session and all its players from the database.`)) return;
  try {
    // First delete all players in the session
    const pd = await apiFetch(`/Players?$filter=session_ID eq '${sid}'`);
    for (const p of (pd.value||[])) {
      await apiFetch(`/Players(ID=${p.ID})`, { method: 'DELETE' });
    }
    // Then delete the session
    await apiFetch(`/GameSessions(ID=${sid})`, { method: 'DELETE' });
    // If we were watching this session, clear the board
    if (sessionId === sid) {
      sessionId = '';
      if (pollTimer) { clearInterval(pollTimer); pollTimer = null; }
      players = [];
      renderBoard();
      document.getElementById('playersList').innerHTML =
        '<p style="font-size:.78rem;color:#a0b8e8">Session deleted.</p>';
      document.getElementById('actionsCard').style.display = 'none';
      document.getElementById('turnLog').innerHTML = '<li>No moves yet.</li>';
      document.getElementById('connStatus').textContent = '✓ Connected';
    }
    await loadSessions();
  } catch(e) {
    alert('Delete failed: ' + e.message);
  }
}

async function joinSession(sid) {
  sessionId = sid;
  document.getElementById('connStatus').textContent = `✓ Connected · session ${sid.substring(0,8)}…`;
  document.getElementById('verifyUrl').value = serviceUrl;
  // Collapse sessions list, hide setup
  document.getElementById('sessionsCard').style.opacity = '0.6';
  document.getElementById('sessionsCard').style.pointerEvents = 'none';
  document.getElementById('setupCard').style.display = 'none';
  // Load game state
  await refresh();
  if (pollTimer) clearInterval(pollTimer);
  pollTimer = setInterval(refresh, 3000);
}

async function refresh() {
  if (!serviceUrl || !sessionId) return;
  try {
    const data = await apiFetch(`/Players?$filter=session_ID eq '${sessionId}'&$orderby=turnOrder`);
    players = (data.value||[]).map((p,i)=>({...p,_colorIdx:i}));
    renderBoard();
    renderPlayers();
    renderActions();
    await refreshLog();
  } catch(e) {
    document.getElementById('connStatus').textContent = '⚠ '+e.message;
  }
}

function renderPlayers() {
  const el = document.getElementById('playersList');
  if (!players.length) { el.innerHTML='<p style="font-size:.78rem;color:#a0b8e8">No players in session.</p>'; return; }
  el.innerHTML = players.map((p,i)=>{
    const color=PLAYER_COLORS[i%PLAYER_COLORS.length];
    const badgeCls = 'badge-'+(p.TurnStatus||'waiting').toLowerCase();
    return `<div class="player-row">
      <div class="avatar" style="background:${color}">${p.name.substring(0,2).toUpperCase()}</div>
      <div class="p-info">
        <div class="p-name">${p.name}</div>
        <div class="p-pos">Square ${p.position} · Roll: ${p.lastRoll??'—'}</div>
      </div>
      <span class="p-badge ${badgeCls}">${p.TurnStatus||'Waiting'}</span>
    </div>`;
  }).join('');
}

function renderActions() {
  const card = document.getElementById('actionsCard');
  const hint = document.getElementById('actionHint');
  const active = players.find(p=>p.TurnStatus==='Playing'||p.TurnStatus==='Moving'||p.TurnStatus==='Blocked');
  if (!active) { card.style.display='none'; return; }
  card.style.display='block';
  hint.textContent = `${active.name} — status: ${active.TurnStatus}`;
  document.getElementById('btnRoll').disabled    = active.TurnStatus!=='Playing';
  document.getElementById('btnConfirm').disabled = active.TurnStatus!=='Moving';
  document.getElementById('btnBlock').disabled   = active.TurnStatus!=='Moving';
  document.getElementById('btnUnblock').disabled = active.TurnStatus!=='Blocked';
  document.getElementById('btnWin').disabled     = !(active.TurnStatus==='Moving'&&active.position===100);
  card.dataset.playerId = active.ID;
}

async function doAction(action) {
  const pid = document.getElementById('actionsCard').dataset.playerId;
  if (!pid) return;
  try {
    await apiFetch(`/Players(ID=${pid})/${action}`, { method:'POST', body:'{}' });
    addLog(`→ ${action} called`, 'normal');
    await refresh();
  } catch(e) {
    addLog(`✕ ${action}: ${e.message}`, 'err');

async function refreshLog() {
  try {
    const data = await apiFetch(`/TurnLog?$filter=session_ID eq '${sessionId}'&$orderby=turnNumber desc&$top=10`);

// Verify service (lightweight client-side checks)

async function runVerify() {
  const url = document.getElementById('verifyUrl').value.trim();
  if (!url) return;
  const rows = document.querySelectorAll('#verifyResults .verify-row');
  rows.forEach(r=>{ r.querySelector('.v-icon').className='v-icon v-pending'; r.querySelector('.v-icon').textContent='…'; });

  async function check(idx, fn) {
    const icon = rows[idx].querySelector('.v-icon');
    try {
      await fn();
      icon.className='v-icon v-pass'; icon.textContent='✓';
    } catch(e) {
      icon.className='v-icon v-fail'; icon.textContent='✕';
      console.warn('Verify check',idx,'failed:',e.message);
    }
  }

  const base = url.replace(/\/+$/,'');
  async function odata(path,opts={}) {
    const isWrite=opts.method&&opts.method!=='GET'&&opts.method!=='HEAD';
    const r=await fetch(base+path,{headers:{'Accept':'application/json',...(isWrite?{'Content-Type':'application/json'}:{})}, ...opts});
    if(!r.ok) throw new Error('HTTP '+r.status);
    return r.json().catch(()=>({}));
  }

  await check(0, ()=>odata('/$metadata'));
  await check(1, async()=>{
    const d=await odata('/Players?$top=1');
    if(!d.value) throw new Error('No Players entity');
    const p=d.value[0]||{};
    if(!('position' in p||'TurnStatus' in p)) throw new Error('Missing fields');
  });
  await check(2, async()=>{
    // Just verify the rollDice action exists in metadata
    const d=await odata('/$metadata');

  });
  await check(3, async()=>{

    const d=await odata('/Players?$filter=TurnStatus eq \'Waiting\'&$top=1');
    const p=(d.value||[])[0];
    if(!p) return; // no waiting player to test against, skip
    const r=await fetch(base+`/Players(ID=${p.ID})/rollDice`,{method:'POST',headers:{'Content-Type':'application/json'},body:'{}'});
    if(r.status!==409) throw new Error('Expected 409, got '+r.status);
  });
  await check(4, async()=>{
    const d=await odata('/BoardSquares?$filter=snakeTo gt 0&$top=1');
    if(!(d.value||[]).length) throw new Error('No snake squares found');
  });
  await check(5, async()=>{
    const d=await odata('/BoardSquares?$filter=ladderTo gt 0&$top=1');
    if(!(d.value||[]).length) throw new Error('No ladder squares found');
  });
  await check(6, async()=>{
    const d=await odata('/BoardSquares?$filter=isDoubleHead eq true&$top=1');
    if(!(d.value||[]).length) throw new Error('No double-head squares found');
  });
  await check(7, async()=>{
    // Verify Blocked status exists in players (or schema supports it)
    const d=await odata('/Players?$top=1');
    if(!d.value) throw new Error('Players not readable');

  await check(8, async()=>{

    const sess=new Set((d.value||[]).map(p=>p.session_ID));

  await check(9, async()=>{
    const d=await odata('/Players?$filter=TurnStatus eq \'Finished\'&$top=1');
    // pass if endpoint is reachable regardless of result
  });
}

How to connect your service

Recommended approach — serve from the same origin as your CAP service:

This avoids CORS issues entirely. Copy index.html into your CAP project's app/ folder:

mkdir -p app
cp index.html app/board.html

CAP automatically serves everything in app/ as static files. Open http://localhost:4004/board.html — the board UI and the OData service are on the same origin so no CORS headers are needed.

add the board.png file in the app/ folder. 

board.png

Then:

  1. Leave the service URL as http://localhost:4004/odata/v4/game
  2. Enter your Session ID (the UUID returned when you created a session in Week 3)
  3. Click Connect — player tokens appear, Roll Dice and Confirm Move work

Alternative — open as a standalone file (file://😞

If you prefer to open index.html directly in a browser without copying it into your project, browsers will block cross-origin requests. Add this to your package.json to allow it:

{
  "cds": {
    "server": {
      "cors": {
        "allowedOrigins": ["*"],
        "allowedHeaders": ["*"]
      }
    }
  }
}

Note: The allowedHeaders: ["*"] wildcard is required — allowedOrigins alone is not enough for preflight requests. Remove both wildcards before deploying to BTP.

For BTP deployments, open the board UI at your deployed URL:

  • https://your-app.cfapps.eu10.hana.ondemand.com/board.html (if copied into app/)
  • or open the local index.html and set the URL to your BTP service endpoint

Tip: The "Verify Service" button in the UI runs 10 quick endpoint checks. For the official 14-check submission validator, use node verify.js <url> (source below).

Part 2: Deploy to SAP BTP (Optional but Recommended)

Deploying makes your service accessible to the Verify Service and lets others watch your game from their browser.

Option A — Cloud Foundry with SQLite (simplest)

Option B — BTP with SAP HANA Cloud

Option C — Keep it local

If you don't have a BTP trial account, that's fine. Run the Verify Service locally:

# In one terminal
cds watch

# In another terminal
node verify.js http://localhost:4004/odata/v4/game

The verify.js script source is provided above in Part 3.

Part 3: The Verify Service

The Verify Service is an automated end-to-end test that validates your entire CAP status-flow implementation.

What it checks

# Check What it validates

1Service reachableGET /$metadata returns 200
2BoardSquares loadedBoardSquares has exactly 100 rows
3Snake squares presentAt least one square with snakeTo > 0
4Ladder squares presentAt least one square with ladderTo > 0
5Double-headed snake squaresAt least 6 squares with isDoubleHead: true
6Create GameSessionPOST /GameSessions returns 201
7Create Player 1POST /Players returns 201
8Create Player 2POST /Players returns 201
9startGame worksPOST /GameSessions(...)/startGame → SessionStatus: InProgress
10First player is PlayingAfter startGame, turnOrder=1 player has TurnStatus: Playing
11Wrong-state rejectionrollDice on #Waiting player returns HTTP 409

Running the verifier

Save the script below as verify.js, then run:

# Run against a local service
node verify.js http://localhost:4004/odata/v4/game

# Run against a deployed BTP service
node verify.js https://your-app.cfapps.eu10.hana.ondemand.com/odata/v4/game

Verify Service — Full Source Code

Copy this entire block, save as verify.js, and run with Node.js 18+:

#!/usr/bin/env node
/**
 * Snake & Ladder Developer Challenge — Verify Service
 *
 * Usage:
 *   node verify.js <service-url>
 *
 * The service URL is your CAP OData v4 root, e.g.:
 *   node verify.js http://localhost:4004/odata/v4/game
 *   node verify.js https://my-app.cfapps.eu10.hana.ondemand.com/odata/v4/game
 *
 * The script creates a clean game session, walks through every status-flow
 * transition, and reports pass/fail for each check.
 */

const BASE = process.argv[2];
if (!BASE) {
  console.error('Usage: node verify.js <service-url>');
  process.exit(1);
}

const root = BASE.replace(/\/+$/, '');
let passed = 0, total = 0;
const results = [];

async function odata(path, opts = {}) {
  const url = root + path;
  const res = await fetch(url, {
    headers: { 'Accept': 'application/json', 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    ...opts,
  });
  const text = await res.text();
  let body;
  try { body = JSON.parse(text); } catch { body = text; }
  return { status: res.status, body };
}

function uuid() {
  return 'xxxxxxxx-xxxx-4xxx-yxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx'.replace(/[xy]/g, c => {
    const r = Math.random() * 16 | 0;
    return (c === 'x' ? r : (r & 0x3 | 0x8)).toString(16);
  });
}

const TOTAL_CHECKS = 14; // update if checks are added/removed

async function check(label, tag, fn) {
  total++;
  const n = String(total).padStart(2, '0');
  const d = String(TOTAL_CHECKS).padStart(2, '0');
  try {
    await fn();
    passed++;
    results.push({ ok: true, label, tag });
    console.log(`  ✓  ${n}/${d} ${label}`);
  } catch (e) {
    results.push({ ok: false, label, tag, err: e.message });
    console.log(`  ✕  ${n}/${d} ${label}`);
    console.log(`       ${e.message}`);
  }
}

async function run() {
  console.log(`\n🐍 Snake & Ladder Verify Service`);
  console.log(`   Target: ${root}\n`);

  await check('Service reachable', 'metadata', async () => {
    const { status } = await odata('/$metadata');
    if (status !== 200) throw new Error(`Expected 200, got ${status}`);
  });

  await check('BoardSquares entity has 100 squares', 'schema', async () => {
    const { status, body } = await odata('/BoardSquares?$count=true');
    if (status !== 200) throw new Error(`Expected 200, got ${status}`);
    const count = body['@odata.count'] ?? (body.value || []).length;
    if (count < 100) throw new Error(`Expected 100 squares, got ${count}`);
  });

  await check('Snake squares present', 'logic', async () => {
    const { status, body } = await odata('/BoardSquares?$filter=snakeTo gt 0');
    if (status !== 200) throw new Error(`Expected 200, got ${status}`);
    if (!(body.value || []).length) throw new Error('No snake squares found');
  });

  await check('Ladder squares present', 'logic', async () => {
    const { status, body } = await odata('/BoardSquares?$filter=ladderTo gt 0');
    if (status !== 200) throw new Error(`Expected 200, got ${status}`);
    if (!(body.value || []).length) throw new Error('No ladder squares found');
  });

  await check('Double-headed snake squares present', 'schema', async () => {
    const { status, body } = await odata('/BoardSquares?$filter=isDoubleHead eq true');
    if (status !== 200) throw new Error(`Expected 200, got ${status}`);
    if ((body.value || []).length < 6) throw new Error('Expected at least 6 double-head squares (3 pairs)');
  });

  const sessionID = uuid();
  const player1ID = uuid();
  const player2ID = uuid();

  await check('Create GameSession', 'entity', async () => {
    const { status } = await odata('/GameSessions', {
      method: 'POST',
      body: JSON.stringify({ ID: sessionID, name: 'Verify Session' }),
    });
    if (status !== 201) throw new Error(`Expected 201, got ${status}`);
  });

  await check('Create Player 1', 'entity', async () => {
    const { status } = await odata('/Players', {
      method: 'POST',
      body: JSON.stringify({ ID: player1ID, session_ID: sessionID, name: 'Verify_Alice', turnOrder: 1 }),
    });
    if (status !== 201) throw new Error(`Expected 201, got ${status}`);
  });

  await check('Create Player 2', 'entity', async () => {
    const { status } = await odata('/Players', {
      method: 'POST',
      body: JSON.stringify({ ID: player2ID, session_ID: sessionID, name: 'Verify_Bob', turnOrder: 2 }),
    });
    if (status !== 201) throw new Error(`Expected 201, got ${status}`);
  });

  await check('startGame → SessionStatus: InProgress', '@to: #InProgress', async () => {
    const { status } = await odata(`/GameSessions(ID=${sessionID})/startGame`, {
      method: 'POST', body: '{}',
    });
    if (status !== 200 && status !== 204) throw new Error(`Expected 200/204, got ${status}`);
    const { body } = await odata(`/GameSessions(ID=${sessionID})`);
    if (body.SessionStatus !== 'InProgress') throw new Error(`Expected InProgress, got ${body.SessionStatus}`);
  });

  await check('After startGame: first player is Playing', '@flow.status', async () => {
    const { body } = await odata(`/Players(ID=${player1ID})`);
    if (body.TurnStatus !== 'Playing') throw new Error(`Expected Playing, got ${body.TurnStatus}`);
  });

  await check('rollDice on Waiting player returns 409', '@from check', async () => {
    const { status } = await odata(`/Players(ID=${player2ID})/rollDice`, {
      method: 'POST', body: '{}',
    });
    if (status !== 409) throw new Error(`Expected 409, got ${status}`);
  });

  await check('rollDice → TurnStatus: Moving, returns integer', '@to: #Moving', async () => {
    const { status, body } = await odata(`/Players(ID=${player1ID})/rollDice`, {
      method: 'POST', body: '{}',
    });
    if (status !== 200) throw new Error(`Expected 200, got ${status}`);
    if (typeof body.roll !== 'number' || body.roll < 1 || body.roll > 6)
      throw new Error(`Expected dice 1-6 in 'roll' field, got ${JSON.stringify(body)}`);
    const { body: p } = await odata(`/Players(ID=${player1ID})`);
    if (p.TurnStatus !== 'Moving') throw new Error(`Expected Moving, got ${p.TurnStatus}`);
  });

  await check('confirmMove → turn rotates to Player 2', 'events', async () => {
    const { status } = await odata(`/Players(ID=${player1ID})/confirmMove`, {
      method: 'POST', body: '{}',
    });
    if (status !== 200 && status !== 204) throw new Error(`Expected 200/204, got ${status}`);
    const { body: p2 } = await odata(`/Players(ID=${player2ID})`);
    if (p2.TurnStatus !== 'Playing') throw new Error(`Expected Player 2 Playing, got ${p2.TurnStatus}`);
  });

  await check('blockPlayer → Blocked; unblockPlayer → $flow.previous', '$flow.previous', async () => {
    await odata(`/Players(ID=${player2ID})/rollDice`, { method: 'POST', body: '{}' });
    const { status: bs } = await odata(`/Players(ID=${player2ID})/blockPlayer`, { method: 'POST', body: '{}' });
    if (bs !== 200 && bs !== 204) throw new Error(`blockPlayer returned ${bs}`);
    const { body: blocked } = await odata(`/Players(ID=${player2ID})`);
    if (blocked.TurnStatus !== 'Blocked') throw new Error(`Expected Blocked, got ${blocked.TurnStatus}`);
    const { status: us } = await odata(`/Players(ID=${player2ID})/unblockPlayer`, { method: 'POST', body: '{}' });
    if (us !== 200 && us !== 204) throw new Error(`unblockPlayer returned ${us}`);
    const { body: restored } = await odata(`/Players(ID=${player2ID})`);
    if (restored.TurnStatus === 'Blocked') throw new Error('Status still Blocked after unblockPlayer');
  });

  console.log(`\n${'─'.repeat(50)}`);
  if (passed === total) {
    console.log(`\n  All ${total} checks passed. 🏆 Challenge complete!\n`);
    const token = Buffer.from(`${root}|${Date.now()}|${passed}/${total}`).toString('base64');
    console.log(`  Verification token:\n  ${token}\n`);
    console.log('  Copy this token into your Week 4 blog comment to claim your badge.\n');
  } else {
    console.log(`\n  ${passed}/${total} checks passed.\n`);
    console.log('  Fix the failing checks and run again.\n');
    process.exit(1);
  }
}

run().catch(e => { console.error(e); process.exit(1); });

A passing verify run outputs:

✓  01/14 Service reachable
✓  02/14 BoardSquares entity has 100 squares
✓  03/14 Snake squares present
✓  04/14 Ladder squares present
✓  05/14 Double-headed snake squares present
✓  06/14 Create GameSession
✓  07/14 Create Player 1
✓  08/14 Create Player 2
✓  09/14 startGame → SessionStatus: InProgress
✓  10/14 After startGame: first player is Playing
✓  11/14 rollDice on Waiting player returns 409
✓  12/14 rollDice → TurnStatus: Moving, returns integer
✓  13/14 confirmMove → turn rotates to Player 2
✓  14/14 blockPlayer → Blocked; unblockPlayer → $flow.previous

  All 14 checks passed. 🏆 Challenge complete!

  Verification token:
  eyJhbGciOiJ...

Copy the verification token and include it in your Week 4 blog comment to claim your badge.

Part 4: AI Plays the Game via CAP MCP

If you connected the CAP MCP server in Week 3, you can now run an AI-vs-AI game. The AI calls your OData actions as MCP tools and narrates the game in real time.

Quick MCP recap: Your srv/game-service.cds must have both annotations on the service:

@mcp
@protocol: ['odata-v4', 'mcp']   // REQUIRED — without this OData drops when @mcp is added
service GameService { ... }

And package.json must have "cds": { "mcp": { "per_action_tool": true } } to expose the 5 unbound wrapper functions as individual MCP tools. The MCP server starts automatically at /mcp/game when cds watch runs.

Example session with Claude( You could us any favourite MCP tool of your choice for the demo)

With the MCP server running and connected to Claude Desktop:

You: "Start a game in session-001 with players Alice and Bob. Play the whole game, taking turns for both players. Narrate each turn like a sports commentator."

Claude will:

  1. Call startGame on the session
  2. Call rollDice for Alice, read her new position, check for snakes/ladders
  3. Call confirmMove, activating Bob
  4. Repeat for Bob
  5. Continue until one player wins, narrating each turn

Example AI narration:

"And we're off! Alice rolls a 4, landing on square 5 — a clean start. Bob rolls a 6, landing on square 7, but wait — square 7 has a LADDER! Bob climbs all the way to square 14! An incredible start for Bob while Alice is still finding her footing at square 5..."

Demo tips

  • Open the Board UI in a browser so you can see the tokens moving as the AI plays
  • Ask Claude to narrate in different styles: sports commentary, dramatic novel, haiku

How to Submit

Reply to the Week 4 blog post on SAP Community with a comment containing:

  1. Your Verify Service token (the base64 string from a passing node verify.js run)
  2. A screenshot of the Board UI showing your game in progress — tokens on the board, turn log visible
  3. A screenshot or curl output showing rollDice returning a roll integer (1–6) and the player's TurnStatus as Moving — confirms Week 2 status-flow transitions work
  4. Optional but celebrated: screenshot sequence of the AI narrating a game

Final Checklist

Make sure your project has:

  • [ ] db/schema.cds with TurnStatus enum and @flow.status on Players
  • [ ] db/schema.cds with SessionStatus enum and @flow.status on GameSessions
  • [ ] srv/game-service.cds with all bound actions annotated with @from / @TO
  • [ ] srv/game-service.js implementing all handlers
  • [ ] db/data/snakeladder-BoardSquares.csv with all 100 squares
  • [ ] At least one multiplayer session with 2+ players in your seed data or test data
  • [ ] The Verify Service passes all 14 checks (node verify.js <url>)

What You Built

Over 4 weeks you built:

Week What you added

1CDS data model, TurnStatus enum, @flow.status annotation, board seed data
2Bound action handlers, snake/ladder logic, HTTP 409 enforcement, $flow.previous
3Turn rotation, session state machine, CAP events, MCP server integration
4Board UI, BTP deployment, Verify Service completion, AI gameplay demo

You've seen the full lifecycle of a CAP status flow: from the CDS annotation that declares valid transitions, through the handler that contains only business logic, to the automatic state management that CAP applies before and after your code runs.

The Snake & Ladder board was the game. The state machine was the point.

entry.title: Custom Business Logic Extensibility in CAP (CDS-Oyster)
entry.content:
You probably already know that you can extend the model of a multi-tenant CAP application (like new fields or entities, UI annotations and translations), but did you know that you can also add tenant-specific custom business logic in a secure way? This session explores what you can do with CDS-Oyster:
CDS-Oyster builds on CAP and MTX-S multi-tenancy by providing a WebAssembly-based sandbox for tenant-specific code. Extension developers can implement custom business logic — entity handlers, actions, event subscribers — without risking the stability or security of the main application.
The sandbox enforces strict limits on memory, execution time, and available APIs. Sandboxed code interacts with the application only through a controlled API layer, preventing unauthorized operations or access to sensitive resources. It coexists alongside regular application-level event handlers.

The last years, my main topics have been model driven software development and extensibility, so CAP is my natural home.
